name: Gerstley Borate
notes: Natural sodium-calcium borate ore (colemanite and ulexite with a hectorite-like clay), long the main low- and mid-fire boron flux in US recipes. The mine closed in 2000; remaining stock is limited and costly, and Gillespie Borate is the recommended pound-for-pound replacement.
manufacturer: Laguna Clay Company (milled from U.S. Borax Gerstley mine ore; mine closed 2000)
hazards: Borate: do not ingest; high-dose animal studies of inorganic borates show reproductive/developmental effects (U.S. Borax Gerstley Borate MSDS, Apr 2013). Avoid breathing dust. Supplier carries a California Prop 65 crystalline-silica warning.

name: Gillespie Borate
notes: Blended borate (mainly ulexite with some colemanite and about 10% clay-like material) made as a pound-for-pound replacement for Gerstley Borate; currently produced and sold in the US, UK and Europe.
manufacturer: Hammill & Gillespie Inc. (Chatham, New Jersey, USA)
hazards: Borate: do not ingest; high-dose animal studies of inorganic borates show reproductive/developmental effects (U.S. Borax Gerstley Borate MSDS, Apr 2013). Avoid breathing dust.

name: Ulexite (Etimine)

manufacturer: Eti Maden (Turkey), sold by Etimine USA Inc. and Etimine S.A.
hazards: Borate: do not ingest; high-dose animal studies of inorganic borates show reproductive/developmental effects (U.S. Borax Gerstley Borate MSDS, Apr 2013). Avoid breathing dust. Etimine's SDS (rev. Oct 2021) lists it as not classified under UN GHS.

name: Alumina Hydrate

hazards: Low hazard nuisance dust; avoid breathing it.
